source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with antisocial personality disorder repeatedly breaks unit rules. What is the best nursing approach?
questions.rationale: Set limits and enforce rules consistently, without anger or punitive responses.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Antisocial PD (PDF p. 264)
questions.quote: Consistent adherence to rules and treatment plan

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: 'You say you want to manage your anger, but you've missed the group meetings.' This nurse response uses:
questions.rationale: Confrontation manages manipulative or deceptive behavior by pointing out inconsistencies.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Antisocial PD (PDF p. 264)
questions.quote: Confrontation – technique designed to manage manipulative or deceptive behavior.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which characteristic is typical of antisocial personality disorder?
questions.rationale: Antisocial PD: violation of others' rights, lying, rationalization, thrill-seeking, irresponsibility.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Antisocial PD (PDF p. 264)
questions.quote: Violation of the right of others

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with borderline personality disorder has cuts on her forearms. What is the nursing priority?
questions.rationale: Recurrent self-mutilation and suicidal gestures make safety the priority.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Borderline PD (PDF p. 264)
questions.quote: Promote client’s safety

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Intense fear of abandonment and unstable relationships suggest which disorder?
questions.rationale: Borderline PD features fear of abandonment, unstable intense relationships, and self-harm.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Borderline PD (PDF p. 264)
questions.quote: Fear of abandonment, real or perceived

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client dresses provocatively at work and constantly seeks attention. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: For histrionic PD, give factual feedback, keep professional distance, and teach social skills.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Histrionic PD (PDF p. 264)
questions.quote: Provide factual feedback about behavior.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with narcissistic personality disorder insults the nurse's competence. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: Use a matter-of-fact approach, do not internalize criticism, and set limits on rude behavior.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Narcissistic PD (PDF p. 264)
questions.quote: The nurse must not internalize such criticism or take it personally

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client avoids social events for fear of criticism and feels inferior. Which disorder?
questions.rationale: Avoidant PD: social discomfort, low self-esteem, hypersensitivity, fear of rejection.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Avoidant PD (PDF p. 265)
questions.quote: They fear rejection, criticism, shame or disapproval

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: What is the main goal for a client with dependent personality disorder?
questions.rationale: Foster self-reliance and teach problem-solving and decision-making skills.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Dependent PD (PDF p. 265)
questions.quote: Foster client’s self-reliance and autonomy

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Repeated hand washing in OCD serves to:
questions.rationale: Compulsions are repetitive acts that attempt to neutralize the anxiety caused by obsessions.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Obsessive-Compulsive (PDF p. 265)
questions.quote: compulsions (repetitive behaviors or mental acts) that attempt to neutralize anxiety

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which finding is expected in a client with anorexia nervosa?
questions.rationale: Anorexia causes amenorrhea, bradycardia, hypotension, hypothermia, and cold intolerance.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Anorexia Nervosa (PDF p. 265)
questions.quote: Amenorrhea

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: What is the initial treatment focus for a severely emaciated client with anorexia?
questions.rationale: Treatment first focuses on weight restoration, rehydration, and correcting electrolytes.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Anorexia Treatment (PDF p. 266)
questions.quote: Weight restoration

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which finding suggests self-induced vomiting in bulimia nervosa?
questions.rationale: Purging erodes dental enamel and causes caries, esophageal tears, and metabolic alkalosis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Bulimia Nervosa (PDF p. 266)
questions.quote: Loss of dental enamel

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Frequent self-induced vomiting in bulimia leads to which acid-base imbalance?
questions.rationale: Vomiting loses gastric acid and causes metabolic alkalosis; laxative diarrhea causes acidosis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Bulimia Nervosa (PDF p. 266)
questions.quote: Metabolic alkalosis (vomiting)

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which nurse attitude is best during meals for a client with an eating disorder?
questions.rationale: Assume a calm, matter-of-fact attitude with positive expectations.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Eating Disorders (PDF p. 266)
questions.quote: Assume a calm, matter-of-fact attitude and positive expectation of the client

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which is a negative (soft) symptom of schizophrenia?
questions.rationale: Negative symptoms include alogia, anhedonia, apathy, flat affect, and avolition.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Schizophrenia (PDF p. 267)
questions.quote: NEGATIVE/SOFT SYMPTOMS

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Schizophrenia requires disturbance in thought and perception for a minimum of:
questions.rationale: Schizophrenia: disturbance for at least 6 months, usually diagnosed in late adolescence or early adulthood.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Schizophrenia (PDF p. 267)
questions.quote: Disturbance in thought process and perception for at least 6 months.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: 'I'll take a pill on the hill if my name is Jill.' This speech pattern is:
questions.rationale: Clang associations link ideas by sound or rhyme rather than meaning.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Schizophrenia (PDF p. 268)
questions.quote: Ideas that are related to one another based on sound or rhyming rather than meaning.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client refuses food, saying the staff poisoned it. This is a:
questions.rationale: Persecutory delusions involve beliefs that others plan to harm, spy on, or poison the client.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Delusions (PDF p. 268)
questions.quote: The client may think that food has been poisoned

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client says the news anchor is sending him private messages. This is:
questions.rationale: Ideas of reference: belief that broadcasts or articles have special meaning for the client.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Delusions (PDF p. 268)
questions.quote: Involve the client’s belief that television broadcasts, music, or newspaper articles have special

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client stops abruptly mid-sentence and cannot continue the idea. This is:
questions.rationale: Thought blocking is abrupt stopping in the middle of a sentence or train of thought.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Changes in Communication (PDF p. 268)
questions.quote: Stopping abruptly in the middle of a sentence or train of thoughts

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client believes others can hear what he is thinking. This is:
questions.rationale: Thought broadcasting: belief that others can hear or know the client's thoughts.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Changes in Communication (PDF p. 268)
questions.quote: A delusion belief that other can hear or know what the client is thinking

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A major depressive episode requires symptoms present nearly every day for:
questions.rationale: Major depression: depressed mood or loss of pleasure for at least 2 weeks.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Mood Disorders (PDF p. 269)
questions.quote: Symptoms must be present every day for 2 weeks

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Which theory attributes depression to believing one has no control over the environment?
questions.rationale: Learned helplessness: mood disorder from the belief that one lacks control.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Mood Disorder Theories (PDF p. 269)
questions.quote: Mood disorder is caused by a belief that one has no control over his environment.
